tasks.title: Recognise a precipitate
tasks.prompt: An insoluble solid appears when two solutions are mixed. What is it?

misconceptions.A flame: The observation is in the solutions, not a flame.
misconceptions.An aqueous ion: Aqueous ions are dissolved; this observation is an insoluble solid.

tasks.explanation: A precipitate is an insoluble solid formed in a reaction.
tasks.hint: Distinguish solid, solution and gas.

tasks.title: Recall cations
tasks.prompt: Which ion is a cation?

misconceptions.Cl⁻: Chloride is a negatively charged anion.
misconceptions.SO₄²⁻: Sulfate is a negatively charged anion.

tasks.explanation: A cation carries positive charge.
tasks.hint: Read the charge sign.

tasks.title: Confirm carbon dioxide
tasks.prompt: Which recorded result supports carbon dioxide?

misconceptions.Bubbles appear: Bubbles show a gas evolved, not which gas.

tasks.explanation: Cloudy limewater is the positive carbon-dioxide test.
tasks.hint: Use the gas test from Testing gases.

tasks.title: Combine ion charges
tasks.prompt: Which neutral formula combines Ca²⁺ with Cl⁻?

misconceptions.Ca₂Cl: Two calcium ions increase the positive imbalance.

tasks.explanation: Two chloride ions balance each calcium ion.
tasks.hint: Match total positive and negative charge.

tasks.title: Read a flame result
tasks.prompt: The supplied clean-wire flame is lilac. Which cation is supported?
tasks.explanation: Potassium gives a lilac flame.
tasks.hint: Name the observed flame colour first.

tasks.title: Keep unresolved candidates
tasks.prompt: Only a white hydroxide precipitate is recorded. Which set remains possible?

misconceptions.Only aluminium: Its excess-reagent dissolution was not observed.
misconceptions.Only copper(II): Copper(II) gives a blue hydroxide precipitate.

tasks.explanation: All three give white; excess reagent is a separate observation.
tasks.hint: Do not invent a missing stage.

tasks.title: Use the excess result
tasks.prompt: The white precipitate dissolves in excess sodium hydroxide. Which cation is supported within the specified set?
tasks.explanation: Only aluminium's precipitate dissolves in excess among these candidates.
tasks.hint: Compare before and excess.

tasks.title: Keep reagents in order
tasks.prompt: What precedes silver nitrate in the specified halide test?

misconceptions.Dilute sulfuric acid: Use the specified nitric acid, not sulfate-bearing acid.

tasks.explanation: Acidify with dilute nitric acid, then add silver nitrate.
tasks.hint: Avoid adding a halide with the acid.

tasks.title: Choose the sulfate chain
tasks.prompt: Which specified chain tests for sulfate?
tasks.answer: Dilute hydrochloric acid, then barium chloride
options: Dilute hydrochloric acid, then barium chloride
Dilute sulfuric acid, then barium chloride
Dilute nitric acid, then silver nitrate
tasks.explanation: A white barium sulfate precipitate is the positive result.
tasks.hint: Match acid, test reagent and solid.

tasks.title: Confirm the evolved gas
tasks.prompt: Acid produces bubbles. Which further result supports carbonate?
tasks.answer: The evolved gas makes limewater cloudy
options: The evolved gas makes limewater cloudy

misconceptions.The solution is colourless: That does not identify the gas.
misconceptions.The gas was not tested: A missing test cannot confirm carbon dioxide.

tasks.explanation: Carbonate plus dilute acid evolves carbon dioxide, confirmed with limewater.
tasks.hint: Bubbles alone are insufficient.

tasks.title: Balance charge as well as atoms
tasks.purpose: Balance charge as well as atoms
tasks.prompt: In Fe³⁺ + __ OH⁻ → Fe(OH)₃, how many hydroxide ions are required?

misconceptions.1: One leaves net 2+ and too few O/H.
misconceptions.2: Two leaves net 1+ and too few O/H.

tasks.explanation: Three hydroxide ions balance Fe³⁺ and supply three OH groups.
tasks.hint: Read the metal charge and product subscript.

tasks.title: Protect the next test
tasks.prompt: Why use separate fresh portions for different chemical tests?
tasks.answer: Previous reagents can contaminate later results
options: Previous reagents can contaminate later results
To change the original ion identities

misconceptions.To change the original ion identities: Each portion starts with the same original sample.
misconceptions.To make every result positive: A test must retain its actual result.

tasks.explanation: Independent portions avoid introducing chloride, sulfate or other interfering reagents from an earlier test.
tasks.hint: Track what has already been added.

tasks.title: Recover crimson
tasks.prompt: Which cation matches a clean-wire crimson flame?
tasks.explanation: Lithium gives crimson; use the named distinction from calcium orange-red.
tasks.hint: Read the controlled flame result.

tasks.title: Recover yellow flame
tasks.prompt: Which cation matches a clean-wire yellow flame in a single-cation set?
tasks.explanation: Sodium gives yellow; distinguish a yellow flame from a yellow silver iodide precipitate.
tasks.hint: Name the observed object.

tasks.title: Recover orange-red
tasks.prompt: Which cation matches a clean-wire orange-red flame?
tasks.explanation: Calcium gives orange-red.
tasks.hint: Keep the two red descriptions distinct.

tasks.title: Recover copper's two tests
tasks.prompt: Which pair distinguishes copper observations?

misconceptions.Blue flame; green hydroxide precipitate: The colours are assigned to the wrong tests.
misconceptions.Brown flame; white hydroxide precipitate: These are not the specified copper observations.

tasks.explanation: Copper gives green flame; copper(II) gives blue hydroxide precipitate.
tasks.hint: Use both the test and observed object.

tasks.title: Recover iron(II)
tasks.prompt: Which cation gives this immediate green hydroxide precipitate?
tasks.explanation: Immediate green precipitate supports iron(II).
tasks.hint: Read the oxidation state.

tasks.title: Recover iron(III)
tasks.prompt: Which cation gives this brown hydroxide precipitate?
tasks.explanation: Brown hydroxide precipitate supports iron(III).
tasks.hint: Read the charge distinction.

tasks.title: Recover bromide
tasks.prompt: Which halide produces a cream precipitate after nitric acid and silver nitrate?
tasks.explanation: Silver bromide is cream.
tasks.hint: Compare all three named solid colours.

tasks.title: Recover iodide
tasks.prompt: Which halide produces a yellow solid after nitric acid and silver nitrate?

misconceptions.Sodium: Sodium gives a yellow flame in a different test.

tasks.explanation: Silver iodide is a yellow precipitate.
tasks.hint: Keep flame and solid distinct.

tasks.title: Recover both-ion reasoning
tasks.prompt: Only a calcium flame result is available. Which conclusion is possible?
tasks.answer: Calcium is supported; the anion and compound remain unknown
options: Calcium is supported; the anion and compound remain unknown
tasks.explanation: A whole compound identity requires evidence for both ions.
tasks.hint: Do not invent the missing anion test.

tasks.title: Read the flame
tasks.prompt: Which cation is supported?
tasks.explanation: Lilac supports potassium in the supplied single-cation set.
tasks.hint: Separate flame observation from ion identity.

tasks.title: Limit a mixture conclusion
tasks.prompt: A mixture gives only a strong yellow flame. What follows?
tasks.answer: Sodium is present; other cations are not ruled out
options: Sodium is present; other cations are not ruled out
The mixture is pure sodium salt

misconceptions.Potassium is absent: No visible lilac does not establish absence in a masked mixture.

tasks.explanation: Flame colours can be masked in mixtures.
tasks.hint: Presence is a narrower conclusion than purity.

tasks.title: Stop before guessing
tasks.prompt: Only the first white result is recorded. What can you identify?
tasks.answer: The cation remains among aluminium, calcium and magnesium
options: The cation remains among aluminium, calcium and magnesium

misconceptions.Aluminium alone: No excess-reagent dissolution has been recorded.
misconceptions.Iron(III): Its specified hydroxide precipitate is brown.

tasks.explanation: Keep all compatible candidates until more evidence exists.
tasks.hint: Read both recorded stages.

tasks.title: Use a second stage
tasks.prompt: Which cation matches white precipitate followed by dissolution in excess?
tasks.explanation: The excess result distinguishes aluminium within this set.
tasks.hint: The two observations belong to the same sodium-hydroxide test.

tasks.title: Retain two candidates
tasks.prompt: The white precipitate remains in excess. Which conclusion is warranted?
tasks.answer: Calcium or magnesium; more evidence is needed
options: Calcium or magnesium; more evidence is needed

misconceptions.Calcium alone: The same two-stage result is compatible with magnesium.

tasks.explanation: Sodium hydroxide alone does not separate calcium from magnesium here.
tasks.hint: Eliminate only a candidate contradicted by the evidence.

tasks.title: Build a halide chain
tasks.prompt: Which result is positive for the requested chloride test?
tasks.answer: White precipitate after nitric acid then silver nitrate
options: White precipitate after hydrochloric acid then silver nitrate
White precipitate after nitric acid then silver nitrate

misconceptions.White precipitate after hydrochloric aci: That acid supplies chloride and contaminates the conclusion.
misconceptions.Lilac flame: This supports potassium, not the chloride anion.

tasks.explanation: The method as well as the colour establishes the test meaning.
tasks.hint: Choose the fresh portion and correct ordered reagents.

tasks.title: Build the sulfate chain
tasks.prompt: Which solid is the positive sulfate-test observation?

misconceptions.A green flame: A flame is a different test.
misconceptions.A colourless gas: The specified sulfate test forms an insoluble solid.

tasks.explanation: Barium sulfate is a white precipitate after the specified acid/reagent chain.
tasks.hint: Keep the solid and flame observations distinct.

tasks.title: Include confirmation
tasks.prompt: Which record confirms the gas in this carbonate test?

misconceptions.Bubbles alone: Gas evolution does not identify the gas.

tasks.explanation: Use the evolved gas's limewater result as well as acid effervescence.
tasks.hint: Track the gas from the acid reaction.

tasks.title: Reject introduced chloride
tasks.prompt: Does this hydrochloric-acid/silver-nitrate result identify chloride originally in the sample?
tasks.answer: No; the acid itself introduces chloride
options: Yes; every white precipitate proves sample chloride
No; the acid itself introduces chloride

misconceptions.Yes; every white precipitate proves samp: The reagent chain contaminates that conclusion.
misconceptions.No; it proves sulfate instead: An invalid chloride test does not identify a replacement ion.

tasks.explanation: Repeat on a fresh portion with dilute nitric acid.
tasks.hint: Find the source of the ion in the reagent.

tasks.title: Conserve atoms and charge
tasks.prompt: Which smallest coefficient of OH⁻ balances this copper(II) equation?

misconceptions.3: Three supplies too many OH groups.

tasks.explanation: Cu²⁺ needs two OH⁻ to form Cu(OH)₂.
tasks.hint: Use the live atom/charge ledger.

tasks.title: Distinguish iron charges
tasks.prompt: Which smallest coefficient of OH⁻ balances iron(III) hydroxide formation?

misconceptions.1: One OH⁻ does not neutralise Fe³⁺.

tasks.explanation: Fe³⁺ + 3OH⁻ → Fe(OH)₃.
tasks.hint: Do not change the fixed species to force a balance.

tasks.title: Use both portions
tasks.prompt: Which supplied single compound matches the paired evidence?

misconceptions.Potassium chloride, KCl: The halide precipitate is cream, not white.
misconceptions.Sodium bromide, NaBr: The flame is lilac, not yellow.

tasks.explanation: Use cation and anion evidence, then combine their charges.
tasks.hint: Do not name a whole salt from one ion test.

tasks.title: Distinguish red flame names
tasks.prompt: A controlled clean-wire flame is crimson. Which cation?
tasks.explanation: Lithium gives crimson.
tasks.hint: Compare the named colours.

tasks.title: Read yellow correctly
tasks.prompt: A controlled single-cation sample gives a yellow flame. Which cation?
tasks.explanation: Yellow flame supports sodium in this controlled record.
tasks.hint: The flame is the observed object.

tasks.title: Use orange-red
tasks.prompt: Which cation matches this controlled orange-red flame?

misconceptions.Copper(II): Green is the copper flame result.

tasks.explanation: Calcium gives orange-red.
tasks.hint: Do not collapse the two red descriptions.

tasks.title: Separate two copper tests
tasks.prompt: What is the copper flame result?
tasks.explanation: Copper flame is green; its hydroxide precipitate is blue.
tasks.hint: Read which test was used.

tasks.title: Identify a blue solid
tasks.prompt: Which cation is supported by the supplied sodium-hydroxide record?
tasks.explanation: Copper(II) gives a blue hydroxide precipitate.
tasks.hint: Name the solid observation.

tasks.title: Keep iron(II) distinct
tasks.prompt: Which cation gives the recorded immediate green hydroxide precipitate?
tasks.explanation: The immediate green precipitate supports Fe²⁺.
tasks.hint: Distinguish charge and precipitate colour.

tasks.title: Keep iron(III) distinct
tasks.prompt: Which cation gives the recorded brown hydroxide precipitate?

misconceptions.Iron(II): Its specified immediate result is green.

tasks.explanation: Brown supports Fe³⁺ in the specified candidate set.
tasks.hint: Use the actual reagent/result pair.

tasks.title: Use dissolution
tasks.prompt: Which cation is supported by white precipitate that dissolves in excess sodium hydroxide?
tasks.explanation: This excess result distinguishes aluminium within the specified set.
tasks.hint: Use both observations.

tasks.title: Keep unresolved pairs
tasks.prompt: White precipitate remains in excess. Which claim is justified?
tasks.explanation: A further observation is needed to distinguish the pair.
tasks.hint: Avoid a stronger conclusion than the record supports.

tasks.title: Match chloride conditions
tasks.prompt: Which requested test chain supports chloride?
tasks.answer: Nitric acid, silver nitrate, white precipitate
options: Hydrochloric acid, silver nitrate, white precipitate
Nitric acid, silver nitrate, cream precipitate
Nitric acid, silver nitrate, white precipitate
tasks.explanation: Chloride gives white silver chloride after the specified reagents.
tasks.hint: The acid matters.

tasks.title: Match bromide conditions
tasks.prompt: Which precipitate supports bromide after nitric acid and silver nitrate?
tasks.explanation: Silver bromide is cream.
tasks.hint: Compare the named halide colours.

tasks.title: Match iodide conditions
tasks.prompt: Which precipitate supports iodide after the specified halide reagents?

misconceptions.Yellow flame: That is a different test, supporting sodium.

tasks.explanation: Silver iodide is a yellow solid precipitate.
tasks.hint: Name colour and physical observation.

tasks.title: Protect sulfate evidence
tasks.prompt: Which acid belongs before barium chloride in the specified sulfate test?

misconceptions.No acid: Use the specified acidified test conditions.

tasks.explanation: Hydrochloric acid then barium chloride gives white barium sulfate if sulfate is present.
tasks.hint: Avoid introducing the target ion.

tasks.title: Require the gas result
tasks.prompt: Which is a complete positive carbonate record in this context?
tasks.answer: Acid effervescence; the gas makes limewater cloudy
options: Acid effervescence; the gas makes limewater cloudy

misconceptions.Acid effervescence only: The evolved gas was not identified.
misconceptions.Gas relights a glowing splint: That supports oxygen, not the carbonate reaction gas.

tasks.explanation: Carbon dioxide confirmation supports carbonate.
tasks.hint: Combine the two observations.

tasks.title: Repair a false flame conclusion
tasks.prompt: How should the contaminated-wire result be treated?
tasks.answer: Repeat with a clean wire; do not identify from the contaminated result
options: Repeat with a clean wire; do not identify from the contaminated result

misconceptions.Report pure sodium salt immediately: The earlier wire contamination prevents that inference.
misconceptions.Report potassium absent: Sodium can mask its flame colour.

tasks.explanation: Cleanliness and known references protect flame interpretation.

tasks.title: Repair the chloride plan
tasks.prompt: What repairs this hydrochloric-acid/halide test?
tasks.answer: Fresh portion, dilute nitric acid, then silver nitrate
options: Fresh portion, dilute nitric acid, then silver nitrate
Add more silver nitrate to the same portion
Name sulfate from the same white precipitate

misconceptions.Name sulfate from the same white precipi: The invalid test does not establish sulfate.

tasks.explanation: Do not try to recover an uncontaminated conclusion from a reagent-contaminated portion.
tasks.hint: Start with the original sample in a fresh portion.

tasks.title: Repair the sulfate plan
tasks.prompt: Why is the sulfuric-acid/barium result invalid for original sample sulfate?
options: A white solid always identifies chloride

misconceptions.A white solid always identifies chloride: Colour alone without test conditions is insufficient.

tasks.explanation: The sulfate may have come from the acid.
tasks.hint: Trace the target ion's source.

tasks.title: Keep fresh samples separate
tasks.prompt: Which proposed plan prevents earlier-reagent interference?
tasks.answer: Separate fresh portions of the original sample
options: One tube receiving every reagent in succession
Keep adding chloride before every test
Separate fresh portions of the original sample
tasks.explanation: Use independent samples for independent evidence.
tasks.hint: A fresh portion has not received another test's reagents.

tasks.title: Reject a premature identity
tasks.prompt: A white first precipitate alone proves which cation?
tasks.answer: It does not uniquely identify aluminium, calcium or magnesium
options: It does not uniquely identify aluminium, calcium or magnesium

misconceptions.Magnesium alone: Aluminium and calcium also produce white.

tasks.explanation: Keep the compatible candidate set.
tasks.hint: A missing excess observation stays missing.

tasks.title: Keep observation and inference distinct
tasks.prompt: Bubbles appear with acid but no gas test is done. Is carbonate confirmed?
tasks.answer: No; the gas identification is missing
options: Yes; every gas bubble is carbon dioxide
No; the gas identification is missing

misconceptions.No; oxygen is therefore confirmed: Missing evidence identifies no replacement gas.

tasks.explanation: Require the limewater observation.
tasks.hint: Do not fill a gap by guessing.

tasks.title: Construct magnesium coefficients
tasks.prompt: Balance the fixed magnesium hydroxide equation using the smallest positive whole numbers.
tasks.explanation: Mg²⁺(aq) + 2OH⁻(aq) → Mg(OH)₂(s). Atoms and net charge balance.
tasks.hint: Keep the species fixed. Count metal, oxygen and hydrogen; match the net charge too. Use the smallest positive whole numbers.

tasks.title: Construct aluminium coefficients
tasks.prompt: Balance the fixed initial aluminium hydroxide formation equation.
tasks.explanation: Al³⁺(aq) + 3OH⁻(aq) → Al(OH)₃(s). Atoms and net charge balance.
tasks.hint: Keep the species fixed. Count metal, oxygen and hydrogen; match the net charge too. Use the smallest positive whole numbers.

tasks.title: Use both ions and charges
tasks.prompt: Which single compound matches the paired records?

misconceptions.Potassium sulfate, KSO₄: That formula has net negative charge.
misconceptions.Potassium bromide, KBr: The anion test is barium sulfate evidence, not silver bromide.

tasks.explanation: Two K⁺ balance one SO₄²⁻.
tasks.hint: Infer both ions before writing the formula.

tasks.title: Use calcium's second evidence
tasks.prompt: Which single compound matches these independent flame and halide records?

misconceptions.Calcium chloride, CaCl: That ratio does not balance charge.

tasks.explanation: Flame identifies calcium; the acidified silver precipitate identifies chloride.
tasks.hint: Use both records and the ion charges.

tasks.title: Leave the unknown anion unknown
tasks.prompt: Only the orange-red flame is known. Can the whole compound be named?
tasks.answer: No; calcium is supported but the anion is unknown
options: Yes; it must be calcium sulfate
No; calcium is supported but the anion is unknown
Yes; it must be calcium chloride
tasks.explanation: One cation result does not identify the whole compound.
tasks.hint: Ask which evidence supports the anion.

tasks.title: Write a sequenced two-ion method
tasks.prompt: A school technician must test a soluble suspected sodium iodide sample using a burner, clean wire, distilled water, dilute nitric acid and silver nitrate. Describe the two tests, their positive results and conclusions. This is an interpretation task, not instructions to try an experiment at home.
tasks.answer: For the cation, a clean wire carrying the sample is placed in a blue/non-luminous Bunsen flame; yellow supports sodium. For the anion, dissolve the sample in distilled water in a fresh test-tube portion, add dilute nitric acid and then silver nitrate solution with a dropping pipette. A yellow precipitate after silver nitrate supports iodide. Distinguish yellow flame from yellow solid and keep both test chains clear.
tasks.explanation: For the cation, a clean wire carrying the sample is placed in a blue/non-luminous Bunsen flame; yellow supports sodium. For the anion, dissolve the sample in distilled water in a fresh test-tube portion, add dilute nitric acid and then silver nitrate solution with a dropping pipette. A yellow precipitate after silver nitrate supports iodide. Distinguish yellow flame from yellow solid and keep both test chains clear.
rubric: Clean sample-bearing wire and blue/non-luminous flame.
Yellow flame linked to sodium.
Dissolve the soluble sample in distilled water in a separate portion.
Dilute nitric acid before silver nitrate solution; suitable dropping pipette.
Yellow precipitate linked to iodide, distinct from a yellow flame.
Two clearly linked, logically sequenced test/result/conclusion chains.
tasks.hint: Write method → observation → conclusion for each ion.

tasks.title: Write a balanced molecular equation
tasks.prompt: Write the balanced equation, with state symbols, for aqueous copper(II) chloride reacting with aqueous sodium hydroxide to form the hydroxide precipitate.
tasks.answer: CuCl₂(aq) + 2NaOH(aq) → Cu(OH)₂(s) + 2NaCl(aq). The copper hydroxide is an insoluble solid; sodium and chloride remain in solution.
tasks.explanation: CuCl₂(aq) + 2NaOH(aq) → Cu(OH)₂(s) + 2NaCl(aq). The copper hydroxide is an insoluble solid; sodium and chloride remain in solution.
rubric: Correct fixed formulas CuCl₂, NaOH, Cu(OH)₂ and NaCl.
Smallest coefficients 1, 2, 1, 2 conserve Cu, Cl, Na, O and H.
Aqueous reactants and sodium chloride; solid copper hydroxide.
Do not change subscripts to balance the equation.
tasks.hint: Count each atom on both sides; show the precipitate state.

tasks.title: Explain the remaining pair
tasks.prompt: Explain why a white hydroxide precipitate remaining in excess cannot by itself distinguish calcium and magnesium. State what further recorded observation would support calcium within that pair.
tasks.answer: Both calcium and magnesium form white hydroxide precipitates that remain in excess sodium hydroxide. A separate clean-wire orange-red flame result supports calcium within this pair. Without that further evidence, retain both candidates.
tasks.explanation: Both calcium and magnesium form white hydroxide precipitates that remain in excess sodium hydroxide. A separate clean-wire orange-red flame result supports calcium within this pair. Without that further evidence, retain both candidates.
rubric: Both candidates share the white/remaining hydroxide result.
The sodium-hydroxide result alone is not unique.
A separate clean-wire orange-red flame supports calcium.
No invented additional result.
tasks.hint: Compare shared evidence with distinguishing evidence.

tasks.hint: Keep the species fixed. Count metal, oxygen and hydrogen; match the net charge too. Use the smallest positive whole numbers.

tasks.title: Construct calcium coefficients

tasks.explanation: Ca²⁺(aq) + 2OH⁻(aq) → Ca(OH)₂(s). Atoms and net charge balance.

misconceptions.Potassium sulfate, K₂SO₄: The blue hydroxide supports copper(II), not potassium.

tasks.title: Independent extended plan
tasks.prompt: Describe a logically sequenced school-test plan to establish copper(II) and sulfate in a suspected soluble copper(II) sulfate sample, using sodium hydroxide, dilute hydrochloric acid and barium chloride. State the separate portions, observations and conclusions.
tasks.answer: Use independent fresh aqueous portions. Add sodium hydroxide to one: a blue precipitate supports copper(II). Acidify a second portion with dilute hydrochloric acid, then add barium chloride solution: a white precipitate supports sulfate. Name each reagent/result/ion chain and do not reuse the first treated portion.
tasks.explanation: Use independent fresh aqueous portions. Add sodium hydroxide to one: a blue precipitate supports copper(II). Acidify a second portion with dilute hydrochloric acid, then add barium chloride solution: a white precipitate supports sulfate. Name each reagent/result/ion chain and do not reuse the first treated portion.
rubric: Separate fresh aqueous portions.
Sodium hydroxide on one portion.
Blue precipitate linked to copper(II).
Dilute hydrochloric acid then barium chloride on the second portion.
White precipitate linked to sulfate.
Clear sequence and no unsupported whole-sample purity claim.

tasks.answer: The yellow flame supports sodium present. Sodium's intense emission can mask other flame colours, so absence of resolved lilac cannot rule out potassium and does not establish purity.

tasks.title: Explain fresh portions
tasks.prompt: Explain why hydrochloric acid is inappropriate before silver nitrate in the halide test, and why repeating on the same treated portion does not repair the inference.
tasks.answer: Hydrochloric acid supplies chloride, which can form a white silver chloride precipitate. The chloride remains in the treated portion, so the original sample's chloride cannot be established from it. Start with a fresh portion and dilute nitric acid before silver nitrate.
tasks.explanation: Hydrochloric acid supplies chloride, which can form a white silver chloride precipitate. The chloride remains in the treated portion, so the original sample's chloride cannot be established from it. Start with a fresh portion and dilute nitric acid before silver nitrate.

Same treated portion remains contaminated.
Fresh original portion with dilute nitric acid then silver nitrate.
